title: And now for a pressing matter....
text:
And now for a pressing matter..... Ironing's a deadly bore
It really is depressing
And when the iron is a dud
It's even more distressing

(This one isn't exactly a dud, but it definitely doesn't live up to my expectations.)

This one seemed like quite a deal
The cord retracts inside it
No dangling wire to trip you up
Because the iron hides it

(A useful feature is the automatic retractable cord reel. You pull out only as much cord as you need, and it winds itself back into the base with the push of a button)

Three steam settings at a touch
There's dry and high and low
It shuts off when it's not in use
Completely apropos

(This model features one button steam settings, and although it's not listed in the manual, automatic shut-off)

A button shoots a misty spray
For when you need things wet
A window shows the water line
That's plain as you can get

The soleplate's coated not to stick
The dial ain't hard to read
From all the specs it seems like this
Is very good indeed

(However)

I filled the iron as they said
I waited for the light
But when I placed it on my shirt
It wasn't watertight

Without a word, or "by your leave"
It leaked from where you fill it
And not until I was half done
Did it refuse to spill it

It's rather heavy at the base
It's neither cute nor sleek
Thank goodness that it's only used
For two hours per week.

Summary: Not the best iron I've used, but with some useful features. The instruction manual lacks troubleshooting suggestions, and although this iron gets hot, it just isn't that cool.

Amanda Richards, June 17, 2008
